concerns.text: FR-018 treats gender as a binary categorical variable and discards any non‑binary entries as missing. This assumption can bias estimates and reduces the effective sample size, potentially threatening the validity of the moderation test. Recommend modeling gender as a multi‑level factor (or including all observed categories) or, at minimum, documenting the impact of this exclusion on the results.

FR-019 specifies that if the homogeneity‑of‑slopes test is significant (p < 0.10) the secondary model becomes the primary analysis. Although pre‑registered, this data‑driven switch can inflate Type I error rates because the decision is based on the same data used for hypothesis testing. Suggest either (a) using a more conservative α for the assumption test, (b) reporting both models without re‑labeling the secondary as primary, or (c) employing a cross‑validation or split‑sample approach to guard against post‑hoc model selection.
